input.area: Public-site card components rendered in lists / grids / rails
components: StoryCard (components/StoryCard.tsx) — <Link> rendering a published standalone story (title, tag pills, excerpt, footer). Shared styles in StoryCard.module.css (the SeriesCard / ChapterCard also import this stylesheet so all three share .card / .title / .tags / .excerpt / .footer rules).
SeriesCard (named export from components/SeriesCard.tsx) — <Link> rendering a series (title, chapter count, status, tags, excerpt, latest-chapter line, like count).
ChapterCard (named export from components/SeriesCard.tsx) — <Link> rendering a single chapter (title, parent-series + part label, tags, excerpt, read time, like count).

ContinueCard (components/ContinueCard.tsx) — <article> wrapping a <Link> + a small remove <button>; shows percent-read badge. Distinct CSS module (ContinueCard.module.css). Used only by ResumeReadingRow.

ContinueReadingRow inline card (components/ContinueReadingRow.tsx) — uses a different inline <Link className={styles.card}> (no separate component file). Renders part label / chapter title / series title from localStorage progress. Styles in ContinueReadingRow.module.css. ResumeReadingRow re-uses this same stylesheet via its own JSX.

HomepageItem (local function inside app/browse/page.tsx) — type-switching wrapper that renders <StoryCard> for type==='story' and <ChapterCard> otherwise. Only used inside ExpandableSection on /browse for the Most Liked / Most Read / Author's Choice rails.

ChapterList row (app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.tsx) — <ol>/<li> list of full-width chapter <Link> rows on the series detail page. Not a typical card-in-a-rail layout — vertical stacked list, each row has part-number badge + body. Flag for review: row hover already exists, but it's a vertical list rather than a horizontal/grid rail; proximity-dock hover may or may not be desired here.
input.currentBehavior: Every card root (StoryCard/SeriesCard/ChapterCard/ContinueCard/ContinueReadingRow inline card) uses a CSS-only hover lift — typically `transform: translateY(-2px)` plus a border-color shift under a `transition: transform var(--transition-fast)` rule. Reveal animation today is a GSAP `gsap.from(cards, { opacity, y, stagger })` triggered once per row by ExpandableSection / CardGrid via useGSAP + ScrollTrigger (see ExpandableSection.tsx lines 30–53 and CardGrid.tsx lines 16–37). There is NO mousemove / proximity hover effect anywhere yet — cards animate only on their own :hover and on scroll-into-view.
input.integrationPoints:
There are five distinct row/grid container DOM nodes that hold cards as direct children — these are the natural mousemove listeners (each card is `containerRef.current.children[i]`, matching the existing GSAP stagger pattern). (1) ExpandableSection.tsx — `
{children}
` (lines 77–82). Used by RecommendationsRow, RelatedSection, and three Browse rails (New Stories / New Series + the Most Liked / Most Read / Author's Choice rails via HomepageItem). The same containerRef toggles between flex row (`.row`) and grid (`.expanded`) — both are valid dock contexts. (2) CardGrid.tsx — `
{children}
` (lines 42–45). Used by /search and /tag/[slug] for the Stories and Series grid sections. (3) ContinueReadingRow.tsx — `
    ` with `
  • ` direct children wrapping `` (lines 34–49). No useRef yet — would need to add one. (4) ResumeReadingRow.tsx — `
      ` with `
    • ` direct children wrapping `` (lines 90–96). Shares ContinueReadingRow.module.css. No useRef yet. (5) app/page.tsx hero `
      ` (lines 72–76) — flex-column of 3 SeriesCards rendered server-side; would need extraction into a tiny client wrapper to attach a ref. The cleanest single hook point is to add a generic ProximityRow / useDockProximity hook applied inside the existing containerRef effect in ExpandableSection + CardGrid + ContinueReadingRow + ResumeReadingRow + a new wrapper on the homepage hero — all share the "ref on container, children are the cards" shape, which is exactly what a GSAP mousemove → distance-to-center → scale transform needs. The cards themselves carry `data-tag-ids` already so adding scale/translate via GSAP `gsap.set(card, { scale, y })` per-frame won't conflict with the existing CSS `transition: transform`-driven hover lift — but be aware of that interaction: the proximity scale and the CSS `:hover { transform: translateY(-2px) }` both write to `transform`, so either move CSS lift into the GSAP timeline or use `gsap.quickTo` with `translate3d`/`scale` while disabling the CSS hover transform on cards inside a proximity-enabled row.
input.notes: Row / grid containers that wrap cards on the PUBLIC site: ExpandableSection (`.row` flex / `.expanded` grid — used on /browse, RecommendationsRow, RelatedSection on /story|/series|/chapter); CardGrid (`.grid` auto-fill grid — used on /search and /tag/[slug]); ContinueReadingRow `.list` (flex row of <li>); ResumeReadingRow `.list` (flex row of <li> wrapping ContinueCard, reuses ContinueReadingRow.module.css); homepage hero `.heroCardsList` (vertical flex of 3 SeriesCards in app/page.tsx). Public-site card-rendering page surfaces: `/` (SeriesCard x3 in hero), `/browse` (ResumeReadingRow + ContinueReadingRow + RecommendationsRow + 5 ExpandableSection rails with StoryCard / SeriesCard / HomepageItem), `/search` (CardGrid of StoryCard + CardGrid of SeriesCard), `/tag/[slug]` (CardGrid of StoryCard + CardGrid of SeriesCard), `/story/[id]` (RelatedSection → ExpandableSection of StoryCard|SeriesCard), `/chapter/[id]` (RelatedSection → ExpandableSection of StoryCard|SeriesCard), `/series/[id]` (RelatedSection → ExpandableSection of StoryCard|SeriesCard; plus ChapterList — vertical row list, separate question whether dock effect applies). Admin paths (app/admin/...) are NOT public and excluded. CommandPalette.tsx imports StoryCard/SeriesCard types but does NOT render those card components — it's a search popover with its own list items, out of scope. Reduced-motion: the existing GSAP code in CardGrid/ExpandableSection bails on `prefersReducedMotion()` from @/lib/gsap — the new proximity hover effect MUST do the same so the dock animation respects accessibility settings.
